title: Imbalanced Data Problem in Machine Learning: A Review
authors: Altalhan, Manahel; Algarni, Abdulmohsen; Turki-Hadjalouane, Monia
tldr: This comprehensive review surveys techniques for addressing class imbalance in ML, covering data-level, algorithm-level, and hybrid approaches with evaluation metrics like F1-score, AUC, and G-mean.
problem_and_motivation: Imbalanced data is a fundamental challenge in machine learning where one class significantly outnumbers others, causing biased classifiers that favor the majority class. This leads to misclassification of minority class instances, which are often critical (e.g., fraud detection, medical diagnosis). Most real-world datasets exhibit this problem, requiring specialized techniques to ensure reliable model performance.
approach: Systematic review of 40 studies from Q1/Q2 journals published 2020-2024.
Categorized techniques into data-level, algorithm-level, and hybrid approaches.
Evaluated oversampling methods (SMOTE, ADASYN, Borderline-SMOTE) and undersampling techniques.
Analyzed cost-sensitive learning, ensemble methods, and algorithm-specific adjustments.
Assessed evaluation metrics including Precision, F1 Score, Recall, G-mean, and AUC.
Identified persistent gaps in generalizability, scalability, and robustness across methods.
findings: SMOTE and variants (Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN) improve minority class representation through synthetic sampling.
Undersampling techniques (Random, Tomek Links, Cluster Centroids) reduce majority class but risk information loss.
Hybrid approaches combining oversampling and undersampling (SMOTEENN, SMOTE-Tomek) provide balanced solutions.
Cost-sensitive learning allocates varying weights to classes, prioritizing minority class misclassification penalties.
Ensemble methods (AdaBoost, Bagging, Random Forests) enhance robustness through multiple classifier combinations.
GAN-based methods generate realistic synthetic samples while maintaining data distribution properties.
Evaluation metrics like AUC-ROC and F1-score are more appropriate than accuracy for imbalanced datasets.
Key limitations include overfitting risk, computational complexity, and challenges with high-dimensional data.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This systematic review provides a comprehensive taxonomy of techniques for addressing class imbalance in machine learning. The three-tier classification (data-level, algorithm-level, hybrid) offers a structured framework for practitioners to select appropriate methods based on dataset characteristics. The identification of key limitations—overfitting risk, computational complexity, and scalability challenges—guides future research directions. The emphasis on appropriate evaluation metrics (AUC-ROC, F1-score over accuracy) establishes best practices for assessing model performance on imbalanced datasets.

limits: Focuses on classification tasks; regression and other ML paradigms not covered.
Most studies use standard benchmark datasets which may not reflect real-world complexity.
Computational overhead of advanced techniques not systematically compared.
Limited discussion on deployment challenges in production environments.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan of all 14 topic domains revealed primary relevance to Domain 12 (Algorithms and Mathematical Foundations). Topic 12.A (Clustering Methods) received high relevance as the paper discusses sampling and balancing techniques applicable to financial data. Topic 12.B (Evaluation of Algorithmic Modules) received high relevance for comprehensive evaluation of ML algorithms and metrics. Topic 12.C (Model Explainability) received medium relevance for addressing interpretability in complex models. Domains 1-11, 13-14 were considered and rejected as the paper focuses on algorithmic techniques rather than Filipino demographics, financial behavioral profiles, expense categorization, predictive modeling in personal finance, budgeting strategies, anomaly detection, mobile design, data privacy, trust mechanisms, savings/debt management, or synthetic data generation.
